title: Tries
summary: Prefix trees share paths so prefix queries cost O(length).

parts.rule: A trie stores strings by sharing one path per character from the root. Insert and prefix search cost O(L) for string length L, not O(number of keys). Each node holds a map or fixed array of next characters plus a flag that marks a complete word ending at that node.

parts.example: Insert "cat", "car", and "do". From the root, edge c leads to a node, then a, then t with an end mark for "cat"; from the a-node an edge r ends "car". Separately, edge d then o ends "do". Prefix query "ca": walk c then a and stop; both "cat" and "car" hang below that node, while "do" does not. Exact query "cap": walk c, a, then find no p child → miss. Insert "cab": from the a-node add edge b with an end mark. body:
Rule. A trie stores strings by sharing one path per character from the root. Insert and prefix search cost O(L) for string length L, not O(number of keys). Each node holds a map or fixed array of next characters plus a flag that marks a complete word ending at that node.

Why it matters. Autocomplete and dictionary-prefix problems explode if every keystroke rescans the whole word list. A hash set answers exact membership but does not efficiently answer "all keys with this prefix." The trie makes the prefix itself the address.

Worked example. Insert "cat", "car", and "do". From the root, edge c leads to a node, then a, then t with an end mark for "cat"; from the a-node an edge r ends "car". Separately, edge d then o ends "do". Prefix query "ca": walk c then a and stop; both "cat" and "car" hang below that node, while "do" does not. Exact query "cap": walk c, a, then find no p child → miss. Insert "cab": from the a-node add edge b with an end mark. Character steps for "cab" equal three, independent of how many other keys share the "ca" stem. For lowercase English letters a length-26 array per node works; for open alphabets use a hash map of children.

When to use. Use a trie for autocomplete, spell-prefix filters, digit or path prefix routing, and word-break search that prunes on missing prefixes. Use it when many keys share stems and queries are prefix-shaped rather than exact-only.

When to refuse. Refuse a trie when you only need exact lookup — a hash set is simpler and enough. Refuse a 26-slot array design for huge Unicode alphabets without compression. Refuse building a trie for one-off searches over a tiny list. Refuse forgetting the end mark and treating every prefix node as a completed word.
